topic_tag: a small press and a poetry movement
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: One historian of the town's literary life argues that the press ______ the plain-spoken regional poetry that flourished there in the 1920s.

worlds.passage: Early in the last century, a one-room press in a river town printed poetry in editions of a few hundred copies. From 1919 its back room had the only stove in town anyone could sit beside for free, and the poets, who had been writing in that style for some years, gathered there nightly to read drafts aloud. The editor, deaf and indifferent to verse, printed their pamphlets exactly as handed to him, and their circle doubled within two years. One historian of the town's literary life argues that the press ______ the plain-spoken regional poetry that flourished there in the 1920s.
worlds.explanation: The poets gathered nightly in the press's back room, so the press "housed" the movement. "Hindered" fails because their circle doubled; "heralded" fails because they had been writing in that style for years before 1919; "guided" fails because the editor, indifferent to verse, printed their work exactly as handed to him.

hindered.why: the movement grew rather than being held back

heralded.quote: had been writing in that style for some years
heralded.why: the press did not announce something that already existed

guided.why: an editor uninterested in verse did not shape it

worlds.passage: Early in the last century, a one-room press in a river town printed poetry in editions of a few hundred copies. It opened in 1919, after the poets had been writing in that style for some years, and its editor, who held that a poem without rhyme was mere prose, owned the only press within a day's travel. The poets, who met in a cafe across the river and went on writing unrhymed verse, saw their first books in print only after his death in 1927. One historian of the town's literary life argues that the press ______ the plain-spoken regional poetry that flourished there in the 1920s.
worlds.explanation: An editor who scorned unrhymed verse owned the only nearby press, and the poets' books appeared only after his death, so the press "hindered" the movement. "Housed" fails because the poets met in a cafe across the river; "heralded" fails because they were already writing before it opened; "guided" fails because they went on writing unrhymed verse.

housed.quote: met in a cafe across the river
housed.why: the movement had its home elsewhere

heralded.quote: after the poets had been writing

guided.why: the poets did not follow its direction

worlds.passage: Early in the last century, a one-room press in a river town printed poetry in editions of a few hundred copies. In 1909 its editor printed a pamphlet calling for poems in the plain speech of the river towns, about farm work and flood seasons rather than nightingales. The press burned the next year, when the poets who would write exactly such poems a decade later were still schoolchildren, and none of them saw the pamphlet until a librarian found it in 1930. One historian of the town's literary life argues that the press ______ the plain-spoken regional poetry that flourished there in the 1920s.
worlds.explanation: The 1909 pamphlet called for the very poetry that arrived a decade later, so the press "heralded" the movement. "Housed" fails because the press burned in 1910; "hindered" fails because the poets were still schoolchildren then, so it obstructed nothing; "guided" fails because none of them saw the pamphlet until 1930.

housed.quote: The press burned the next year
housed.why: a press gone before the movement could not be its home

hindered.why: it could not obstruct poets who had not yet begun

guided.quote: none of them saw the pamphlet
guided.why: poets who never read its call were not steered by it

worlds.passage: Early in the last century, a one-room press in a river town printed poetry in editions of a few hundred copies. It opened in 1919, when the poets were already writing about farm work and floods but still in the ornate meters of their schooling, and its editor answered every manuscript with pages of notes urging plain speech to match plain subjects. The poets, who met in a cafe across the river, rewrote along those lines, and a city firm brought out their books to quick success. One historian of the town's literary life argues that the press ______ the plain-spoken regional poetry that flourished there in the 1920s.
worlds.explanation: The editor's notes urged plain speech, and the poets rewrote along those lines, so the press "guided" the movement. "Housed" fails because the poets met in a cafe and published with a city firm; "hindered" fails because their books met quick success; "heralded" fails because they were already writing about those subjects when it opened.

housed.quote: met in a cafe across the river
housed.why: the press was not the movement's home

hindered.why: the movement was not held back

heralded.why: the movement had begun before the press, so it did not announce it in advance
